overview: The committee approved space allocations and programmatic designs for dining services, the Curtis Tufts program, and the Early Childhood Center. Discussions focused on balancing operational needs and reimbursable square footage for the new high school building.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the August 25, 2026 meeting minutes with an amendment to include 500 parking spaces as a critical decision point for debt consideration.

items.title: Budget Update and Approval of Invoices
items.summary: Approved August invoices totaling $115,000 for Left Field and SMMA after reviewing the remaining feasibility study budget of approximately $226,370.

items.title: Dining and Food Service Review
items.summary: Approved the dining and food service layout, which includes a scramble-style servery, a 400-square-foot quiet dining room, and a cafe snack shop in the media center. The committee discussed the necessity of the larger servery for operational efficiency and the sustainability benefits of dedicated dishwashing space.

items.title: Curtis Tufts Programmatic Review
items.summary: Approved the Curtis Tufts program layout with a request to further investigate classroom sizes; the plan consolidates the program into approximately 6,000 net square feet within the high school. Members discussed the benefits of moving the program from its current isolated building to allow for better student access to CTE programs and shared facilities.

items.title: Medford Early Education Program (MEEP)
items.summary: Approved several space reductions for the Early Childhood Center, including the removal of a playroom and two breakout rooms and a reduction in laundry space. A motion to eliminate the MEEP program from the high school project entirely was denied after committee members debated centralization versus neighborhood-based preschool models.

items.title: Design Update and Future Schedule
items.summary: Reviewed the upcoming design schedule for site massing and exterior building features and announced a sustainability-themed community forum for September 17.

subject: High School Programmatic Design Approvals
